question.problem:
The concentration of a medication in a patient's bloodstream, measured in milligrams per liter, is given by the function $C(t)$, where $t$ is the time, in hours, since the medication was taken. The values of $C(t)$ for different values of $t$ are given in the table below:

| $t$ | $1$ | $5$ | $9$ | $14$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $C(t)$ | $18$ | $11$ | $7$ | $2$ |

Approximate the rate of change of the concentration when $t=9$ using a backward difference approximation. Do not round the answer.

The estimated rate of change when $t=9$ is
{{field-1}} milligrams per liter per hour.

current_example.problem:
A race car's position along a straight track, measured in meters from the starting line, is given by the function $s(t),$ where $t$ is the time in seconds. The values of $s(t)$ for different values of $t$ are given in the table below.

| $t$ | $1.2$ | $1.4$ | $1.6$ | $1.8$ | $2.0$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $s(t)$ | $1.3$ | $2.7$ | $2.9$ | $3.5$ | $5.0$ |

Approximate the velocity $s'(t)$ when $t=1.6$ using a backward difference approximation.
current_example.worked_solution:
We use the backward difference approximation formula

$$
s'(t) \approx \frac{s(t) - s(t-h)}{h}
$$

 

at the time $t=1.6.$ We choose the step size $h$ to be as small as possible, in this case $h=0.2.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{s}^{′}(1.6) & ≈\frac{s(1.6)-s(1.6-0.2)}{0.2} \\  & =\frac{s(1.6)-s(1.4)}{0.2} \\  & =\frac{2.9-2.7}{0.2} \\  & =\frac{0.2}{0.2} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

So at the time $t=1.6,$ the velocity is approximately $1\, \textrm{m}/\textrm{s}.$
